name: San Vicente Coatlán Zapotec
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. 2008. Un estudio comparativo de los tonos del zapoteco sureno — comparative Southern Zapotec prosody study covering San Vicente Coatlan Zapotec

sources.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. 2014. Algunos rasgos lingüísticos del zapoteco sureño. In R. Barriga Villanueva & E. Herrera Zendejas (eds.), Lenguas, estructuras y hablantes: estudios en homenaje a Thomas C. Smith Stark, vol. 2, pp. 643-659+. México: El Colegio de México. (author scan, no text; scanned here)
sources.note: Group-level only: defines 'macrocoatecano' to include SVC Zapotec (pp.644-645); pp.654-655 'Elisión de vocales átonas': Southern Zapotec lost unstressed vowels historically, roots/words tend to be monosyllabic (strongly so in macrocoatecano), new unstressed syllables arise in Spanish loans and compounds and differ from tonic syllables by lacking tonal contrasts. No stress-position rule for SVC specifically.

sources.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. 2023. Realis morphology and Chatino's role in the diversification of Zapotec languages. Diachronica 40(4):439-491 (author preprint).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Historical only: 'In most varieties of Southern Zapotec, pre-tonic vowels have reduced or deleted, creating initial clusters'; cites one SVC form /m-tek/ from Klotz 2019 (SVC dictionary, Ms.). No synchronic SVC stress rule.

sources.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. 2019. Southern Zapotec verb classes. Amerindia 41:121-165 (author copy).
sources.note: No SVC data; only a passing remark that these languages delete or reduce unstressed vowels.

sources.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. 2014. Algunas isoglosas de la Sierra Sur (COLOV VI slides); 2018. La inteligibilidad y la autodenominación en la clasificación de lenguas zapotecas de la Sierra Sur y más allá (INALI coloquio handout).
sources.note: Classification only (SVC + Coateco = 'coatecano'); one segmental isogloss for SVC (VV sequence where Coateco has an open vowel); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. 2008. Un estudio comparativo de los tonos del zapoteco sureño. In A. López Cruz & M. Swanton (eds.), Memorias del Coloquio Francisco Belmar, vol. II, pp. 161-185. Oaxaca: Biblioteca Francisco de Burgoa.
sources.note: Names SVC Zapotec (p.162) as part of 'el coateco mayor' but uses NO SVC data (five variants: S.Miguel/Sta María Coatlán, S.Baltazar Loxicha, S.Agustín Mixtepec, S.Bartolomé Loxicha, S.Agustín Loxicha). p.163: all Southern Zapotec languages lost unstressed (post-tonic) vowels; pp.167-168 describe tonal behaviour of unstressed syllables in Miahuatec only. The earlier scan's 'source named' is thus reachable but not a source for SVC stress.

sources.citation: Wagner, W. John. 2008 [file dated 2009]. Pronouns in San Vicente Coatlán Zapotec. SIL-Mexico Branch Electronic Working Papers #003. 18 pp. (SIL archive 10696).
sources.note: Nothing. Pronoun description only (intro: Southern Zapotec, ~4,000 speakers, VSO); no phonology/orthography section; no mention of stress, accent or tone anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent + reading).

sources.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. 2004. A Coatlán-Loxicha Zapotec Grammar. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley.
sources.note: About CLZ, not SVC: SVC is CLZ's closest relative, once part of a dialect continuum (p.7 fn.3); CLZ itself has final stress in polysyllables (§2.2.3, pp.81-88). No statement about SVC stress.

tone.summary: Says nothing about tone; a 7-page story reader in San Vicente Coatlán Zapotec with a Spanish summary and colophon. The story text carries no tone diacritics or tone numbers.

sources.citation: Wagner, W. John / SIL Mexico. Unpublished phonology or orthography statement for San Vicente Coatlán Zapotec (SIL fieldwork since 1996; an orthography with tone marking is in use in ~30 literacy titles).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL teams normally file a phonology write-up before producing primers; would contain the stress statement; ask SIL-Mexico archives (John_Wagner@sil.org given in Wagner 2008).

sources.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. In preparation. Zapotecan Stress and its Interaction with Phonological Contrasts. (cited in Beam de Azcona 2023, J. Historical Linguistics preprint)

sources.note: Family-wide stress study by the specialist who has SVC field data (consultant from San Vicente Coatlán cited in her 2004 grammar); the most likely place for an explicit SVC stress statement.

sources.citation: Klotz, Robert. 2019. Dhiksiyonarr dhīxh-nde'e - dhīxh-xtīl - dhì'ixh ingles. Diccionario del zapoteco de San Vicente Coatlán / San Vicente Coatlán Zapotec dictionary. Ms.

sources.note: Only lexical documentation of SVC cited in the literature (Beam de Azcona 2023); a dictionary front matter typically explains tone/stress marking; would show whether polysyllables are final-stressed as in Coatlán-Loxicha Zapotec.
